newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR condemns killings in eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR condemns killings in eastern Zaire.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday it had received "increasingly shocking reports" of killings of refugees around Kisangani and other areas of eastern Zaire held by rebel troops, and called for a full investigation.

Spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole, speaking to a news briefing, said the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) condemned the abduction by armed soldiers of 50 children and 60 adults from a hospital near Bukavu at the weekend.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila agreed on Sunday to give aid agencies access to 100,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees who fled camps in his territory when they came under armed attack last week.

"While we appreciate the promise of the Alliance leader, Laurent Kabila, to help us locate and repatriate the refugees, we are receiving increasingly shocking reports of killings of refugees both in the area around Kisangani and elsewhere," O'Toole said.
"There are lots of reports from refugees about them being attacked by villagers or even by Alliance troops," she added. "These killings must stop and an urgent investigation must be launched."

UNHCR estimated up to 10,000 refugees may now be in Bairo but said Alliance troops at a crossing point had only allowed through three of 11 trucks heading to the site with food and to transport the refugees to Kisangani for airlifting to Rwanda.
